LESSON: CHANGE OF STATE

Grade: Grade 6
Subject: SCIENCE & TECHNOLOGY
Strand: MATTER
Topic 2.1: Change of State

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Change of State. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: How is change of state of matter important in day-to-day life?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. identify the changes of state when substances are heated or cooled
2. describe the applications of the change of state of matter in everyday life
3. appreciate the applications of change of state of matter in day-to-day life

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: CHANGE OF STATE
Subject: SCIENCE & TECHNOLOGY · Grade: Grade 6
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Change of State helps you succeed in SCIENCE & TECHNOLOGY. You will understand it, practise it, and use it in your school compound, home, farm, or county.

KEY FACTS: CHANGE OF STATE
Study Change of State like a learner textbook page: meaning → examples → practice → check.
Replace teacher words with your own words.
If a step is unclear, rewrite it shorter and try again.

PART 1: Identify the changes of state when substances are heated or cooled

What this means
In this part you learn to identify the changes of state when substances are heated or cooled. You will use ideas from in your school compound, home, farm, or county.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: identify the changes of state when substances are heated or cooled.
2. Observe, explain, then apply using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Observe: Name what you can see/touch about “Change of State” around your school.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can identify the changes of state when substances are heated or cooled. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Describe the applications of the change of state of matter in everyday life

What this means
In this part you learn to describe the applications of the change of state of matter in everyday life. You will use ideas from in your school compound, home, farm, or county.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: describe the applications of the change of state of matter in everyday life.
2. Observe, explain, then apply using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Explain: Say why Change of State matters for health, safety, or the environment in Kenya.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can describe the applications of the change of state of matter in everyday life. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 3: Appreciate the applications of change of state of matter in day-to-day life

What this means
In this part you learn to appreciate the applications of change of state of matter in day-to-day life. You will use ideas from in your school compound, home, farm, or county.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: appreciate the applications of change of state of matter in day-to-day life.
2. Observe, explain, then apply using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Apply: Describe one safe action you can take related to Change of State this week.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can appreciate the applications of change of state of matter in day-to-day life. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Change of State is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Name what you can see/touch about “Change of State” around your school. (skill: identify the changes of state when substances are heated or cooled)

Example 2: Say why Change of State matters for health, safety, or the environment in Kenya. (skill: describe the applications of the change of state of matter in everyday life)

Example 3: Describe one safe action you can take related to Change of State this week. (skill: appreciate the applications of change of state of matter in day-to-day life)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Change of State to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: identify the changes of state when substances are heated or cooled.
3. Practise this skill: describe the applications of the change of state of matter in everyday life.
4. Practise this skill: appreciate the applications of change of state of matter in day-to-day life.
5. Make one local Kenya example of Change of State from your county, market, farm, or school.
6. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Change of State: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 6 learner study Change of State?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. How is change of state of matter important in day-to-day life?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Change of State means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: identify the changes of state when substances are heated or cooled.
5. Be able to: describe the applications of the change of state of matter in everyday life.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
